For integers k >1 we study the existence of labelings satisfying the following condition: Every residue class modulo k occurs exactly \\\\cell n\\\\k\\\\cell or \\\\floor n\\\\k \\\\floor times in the sequence c(v_1),...,c(v_n) and exactly \\\\cell m\\\\k \\\\cell or \\\\floor m\\\\k \\\\floor times in the sequence c*(e_1),...,c*(e_m). Hypergraph H is called k-cordial if it admits a labeling with these properties. Hovey [Discrete Math. 93 (1991), 183{194] raised the conjecture (still open for k > 5) that if H is a tree graph, then it is k-cordial for every k. Here we investigate the analogous problem for hypertrees (connected hypergraphs without cycles) and present various su±cient conditions on H to be k-cordial. From our theorems it follows that every k-uniform hypertree is k-cordial, and every hypertree with n or m odd is 2-cordial.
